title: Dose shampoo from a flip-top bottle: flip the cap open, squeeze 1.5-4 g into a dish, snap it shut
instruction: Put a coin-sized dose of shampoo in the dish, then close the bottle.
context: Dosing shampoo from a flip-top bottle is an everyday bathroom job; the dish stands in for the palm the dose goes into, as when helping someone wash their hair. Mental Floss, citing dermatologist Dr. Debra Jaliman: "a quarter-sized amount of shampoo is indeed appropriate", and Keune says a 1 euro coin's worth is sufficient for short to medium-length hair. The flip cap is a snap: its lid is held shut until the thumb tab is lifted past the catch, and below 61 degrees open it lies over it, so a lid only cracked onto its catch sends the shampoo over the cap. Flipping it over upright takes up to 0.38 N sideways at the cap, more than the 0.21 N that tips the free bottle, so one hand steadies it while the other works the lid. Held open cap-down it does not run until squeezed: a light squeeze gives nothing, a firm one a dose that grows while held, so the walls must be squeezed and let go in time. The lid must snap back past its catch, not stay open or on it.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases, x forward, y to the robot's left, heights above the counter (the station table). Room at 20 to 24 C. A US quarter lies on the pad beside the dish as a size reference. Bottle: Suave Professionals Rose Oil Infusion Volumizing Shampoo, 12.6 fl oz (373 mL), the same product and scent for every trial (Target listing), 7.14 x 4.28 x 21.27 cm with its cap shut (the listing's 2.812 x 1.687 x 8.375 in), half used: 200 mL (206 g) of shampoo, filled to a pen line on the label, 234 g in all with the 28 g empty bottle. Before first use it is opened and held cap-down over a cup for 60 s unsqueezed: nothing comes out, as in the simulation (else use another bottle). Its cap is a snap flip-top, as the maker's photos show. It stands upright with its base's middle at (30.0, 5.0), its 7.14 cm width along x; flip-top cap 34 mm across, its base 20.7 mm tall and its lid 12 mm, a 4 mm orifice, the lid hinged on the cap's left (+y) edge with a thumb tab sticking out 5 mm on the right (cap sizes from the maker's photos; the open stop is at 115 degrees). The lid is snapped shut. Dish: a round porcelain dip bowl, 8.9 cm across, 2.5 cm tall, 8.1 cm inside, 110 g, standing at (30.0, -5.0), empty and dry. The bottle and dish stand on a flat, taped, plastic-backed absorbent bench pad (about 50 x 60 cm) on the counter, so the simulated counter still matches. After each reset the bottle stands upright, lid shut, for 5 minutes before the trial. Both arms start at their ready pose, grippers open.
scoring: Grams of shampoo in the dish (in simulation mL x 1.03 g/mL). 1.0: 1.5 to 4.0 g in the dish (a coin-sized dose), at most 0.3 g anywhere outside it (counter, dish rim and outside, the cap, the lid, the bottle's outside), the lid clicked shut (past its catch), the bottle and the dish standing upright (within 15 degrees) on the counter, let go (every arm link at least 5 mm from them in simulation), all still (under 1 cm/s) for 1 s. 0.5: the dose and no drips, but not that finish: the cap left open or resting on its catch, the lid held down by a hand, the bottle still held or not standing. 0.25: 0.5 to 1.5 g or 4.0 to 15 g in the dish (as from a squeeze held too long or too hard), or 0.5 to 15 g in the dish with more than 0.3 g outside it. 0: under 0.5 g or over 15 g in the dish; doing nothing scores 0 (the dish starts empty), as do holding the open bottle cap-down without squeezing or with only a light squeeze (the orifice opens only above 3.06 kPa; nothing comes out), squeezing with the cap shut (nothing comes out), squeezing through a lid opened less than 61 degrees (where its tab end starts to uncover the orifice; below it the lid lies over the orifice: the shampoo runs over the cap and counts as outside), a dumped dose, and the dish knocked over (its shampoo counts as spilled). Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0. Real trial, judged by eye from the overhead video (no scale or gauge), with a US quarter (24 mm) beside the dish as a size reference; the dose is the dollop in the dish, its width read in the first overhead frame after the bottle last leaves the dish, before it spreads (24 mm domed 6 mm is 1.5 g; a wider dollop slumps lower, and 34 mm domed 8 mm is 4.0 g; an approximation). Same tiers: 1.0: a dollop 24 to 34 mm across, no drop outside the dish, and at the end the lid flush on the cap, the bottle and dish upright on the pad, both hands off and clear, nothing moving over the last second. 0.5: that dollop with no drop outside, but the lid open or on its catch (visibly open), a hand still on the lid or bottle, the bottle not standing, or something still moving. 0.25: a dollop at least a dime's width (18 mm, about 0.6 g) and not across most of the dish's floor that is narrower than a quarter or wider than 34 mm, or has any drop on the pad, the dish's rim or outside, the cap, the lid or the bottle. 0: nothing in the dish or less than a dime's width, shampoo across most of the dish's floor (a dumped dose), or the dish knocked over; doing nothing scores 0.
reset_notes: Wash and dry the dish, wipe the cap's orifice and lid with a damp, then a dry paper towel, replace the bench pad if wet, snap the lid shut and stand the bottle and dish on their tape marks. Once the shampoo is a finger's width under the pen line, top it up to the line from the same product, then let it stand 30 minutes. A gripper finger's nitrile glove that tears or gets shampoo on it is replaced; the folded glove fingers and tape stay clear of the pads, the fingertips and the wrist camera. Stand the bottle upright, lid shut, 5 minutes before the next trial. About 3 minutes plus the rest. Each trial uses about 2 to 3 g of shampoo and a paper towel; nothing else is consumed.
fidelity: Rigid bodies. The broad walls are sprung panels; shampoo is a flow model, not a fluid: the walls' squeeze compresses the air inside and, with the shampoo's weight (at most 1.16 kPa), must pass the orifice's 3.06 kPa opening pressure (a shampoo valve patent's); flow from an unclicked orifice within 70 degrees of down, onto the cap while the lid is under 61 degrees open, else plumb. The lid's snap is an angle-only spring on its hinge; wall, flow, valve and snap values are model choices (README).
scores: Dream-1 run: 0 (2,400 steps; the arms drew back and never reached the bottle); demo: 1.0 (1,079 steps, 2.64 g). Cheats: open cap-down 45 s unsqueezed 0 (0 g), light squeeze 5 s 0 (0 g), cap left open 0.5, lid held on its catch 0.5, squeezed shut 0, walls fully in 10 s 0 (15.5 g), nothing 0
